Read ext/Ask (Ask.js, pick.js, chat.js, reply.js, ask.css, readme.md, doc/decisions.md, doc/reply.md), layouts/browse/ (verdicts.js the seam, page.js, items.json), the approved page, and the layout skill's approved-set bullet. items.json check: 0 of 102 browse ids contain '/', every page url does — the two keyspaces can never collide by construction.

Found a real trap before writing any code: Router.js loads first, pushes history.pushState second, and activate() sets router.active AFTER calling every page's own content()/render() — so location.pathname and app.router.active.url both still name the PREVIOUS page while a page's own content() is running. Page.url (set once, at declare time) is the only safe source. Documented loudly on verdict_mark()'s own doc comment and in ext/Ask/doc/decisions.md.

Built public/framework/ext/Ask/verdict.js: verdict_mark(url) and verdict_acts({url, m, about}). Reuses /layouts/browse/verdicts.js's own Verdicts singleton and file (public/layouts/verdicts.jsonl) rather than a second store — one owner-approved library, not one per realm (the alternative, and why it loses, is in doc/decisions.md). Improve's note is the verdict's own note field by default; passing an optional task manifest m also opens reply.js's reply() under it, so a note CAN reach Claude the same way a reply does, for a page that has a task log to file into.

Wired verdict_mark/verdict_acts into chat.js's mount({app, task, url, ...}) — the mark builds immediately (visible without opening the panel), the buttons build lazily inside the panel like chat() already does. Added .ask-verdict-* rules to ask.css, matching browse's .std-browse-mark colour convention (is-approve/is-improve).

While building: the sibling edit-mode minion landed ext/Ask/edit.js mid-task and Ask.js's available() became `return edit();`. My verdict controls already gated on available() per the brief, so the edit switch applies for free — no second change needed. Updated verdict.js's own doc comment (it had a forward-looking TODO for exactly this) to say so instead of describing it as pending.

mount({app: this.app, url: this.url}) added to the ten named pages: layouts/practice/catalog, layouts/practice/reader, layouts/practice/workbench (content()); layouts/shell (own render(), a sibling of .std-shell-view, fixed position so it never touches the shell's height contract); layouts/labs/blogx, labs/decks, labs/screens, labs/sections, labs/shells (content()); layouts/labs/mag (own column(), placed OUTSIDE the cover's whole-page <a> on purpose so the ? never fires the cover link).

Layout skill: fixed the now-stale /imagine/design/layout/approved/ link in 'The approved set is closed' (would have 404'd) and added the required clause pointing at the live library, with a dated note on the move.
Started the private server, PORT 8137, background — real Windows PID via netstat: 31728 (bash's own $! is not trustworthy in this git-bash on Windows).

Playwright headless crawl (NODE_PATH to the global playwright install, no repo dependency added): zero console errors at 400/1280/3440 on three of the ten mounted pages — layouts/practice/workbench/, layouts/shell/, layouts/labs/mag/ (the two riskiest patterns: own render() and own column(), plus the required workbench proof page).

Round trip on layouts/practice/workbench/: opened the floating ?, pressed Approve for real, the control's own mark read class="ask-verdict-mark is-approve" — the write and the live redraw both work. Checked /layouts/browse/practice-workbench/'s own mark: it does NOT show this verdict, confirmed and expected — browse keys by its catalogue id, this control keys by the page's own url, two keys in one file by design (doc/decisions.md says why).

BUG the proof caught: the approved library showed nothing for the real approve, even though library_data() correctly returned it (proved with a debug print: {connected: false, list: [1 item]}). Cause: library()'s first draw checked $box.el.isConnected, but that box is built synchronously inside content(), before core inserts the page's view into the document — a fast-resolving fetch can beat the mount. browse/page.js's OWN live() only checks isConnected on the WATCH-triggered redraw, never on the first one; my verdict.js copy had put the same guard on the first draw too. Fixed both files to match browse's real split; re-ran the proof: the library now shows the approved workbench link. This bug would also have silently hidden verdict_mark() on a fresh page load whenever an earlier verdict already existed and the socket answered fast — worth flagging for skill-improvement.

Cleaned up the test write from public/layouts/verdicts.jsonl (the owner is the only writer) — deleted the one line this proof appended, re-verified the file no longer carries it, and confirmed the mark/library both go back to unjudged.
